breaking.change: device.json's `measured.device.gpu` is removed: it came from a second adapter the page asked for, which was not always the one the game drew on (Chrome on an NVIDIA host answers a request without a power preference null). `measured.adapter` names the renderer's own adapter.
breaking.fix: Read `measured.adapter` (such as `nvidia/lovelace`, or `google/swiftshader (software)` on CPU WebGPU) instead of `measured.device.gpu`.

added.summary: On the web, the performance record (`perf report`, the shell's `perf()`) names the WebGPU adapter its times were measured on: `json.adapter` and its text's first line, `vendor/architecture` with ` (software)` on a CPU rasterizer (the fallback adapter, SwiftShader, llvmpipe, lavapipe), so a time measured on CPU WebGPU is never read as a GPU's. The web trace's `otherData.adapter` names it too.
Its summary line, `--json` line, report.md and device.json name the adapter the frames were timed on (`chrome: webgpu on google/swiftshader (software), first frame …`).
